skills.label: Finding explicit information
skills.description: Locate and accurately paraphrase details stated in the passage, including dates, lists and comparisons.
skills.tip: Choose an anchor word, find its sentence, then check the surrounding lines before selecting your answer.

skills.label: Recognising contradictions
skills.description: Identify passage evidence that directly conflicts with a statement rather than treating missing information as false.
skills.tip: For False, point to the exact evidence that makes the statement impossible. Missing evidence alone is not enough.

skills.label: Spotting unsupported claims
skills.description: Recognise when the passage leaves a claim unresolved, including unstated comparisons, intentions and historical firsts.
skills.tip: Ask whether both the statement and its opposite could fit the passage. If they could, the information is missing.

skills.label: Drawing supported inferences
skills.description: Combine passage facts or apply a stated relationship to reach a conclusion without adding outside assumptions.
skills.tip: Write the two passage facts that support your conclusion. Remove any step that needs an unstated assumption.

skills.label: Reading qualifiers and scope
skills.description: Preserve the strength, extent and time frame of claims such as some, most, all, only, may and always.
skills.tip: Compare the strength of the wording in the question and passage. Some does not prove all, and may does not mean always.

skills.label: Understanding viewpoints
skills.description: Distinguish the narrator’s position from reported opinions and identify the tone or stance of a named source.
skills.tip: Track who holds each view. A claim attributed to a researcher is not automatically the narrator’s conclusion.

skills.label: Main idea and purpose
skills.description: Identify the passage’s central message and explain why an example, contrast or detail is included.
skills.tip: Summarise each paragraph in a few words, then choose the option that captures its role without adding a new claim.

skills.label: Evaluating evidence
skills.description: Assess what observations support, challenge or leave uncertain about an explanation, including the impact of new findings.
skills.tip: Separate an observation from the explanation built on it. Ask what the new evidence actually changes, and what it leaves unresolved.

skills.label: Meaning in context
skills.description: Interpret a word, reference or phrase using the surrounding passage rather than its everyday meaning alone.
skills.tip: Read the whole sentence and its neighbours. Substitute the proposed meaning or referent and check that the logic still works.
